The unsolicited kindnesses I have received from my country, through the channel of your excellency, demand my warmest acknowledgments, and I pray you, sir, to accept the same, together with the assurances of that high respect and esteem with which I have the honor to be,

Your most obedient and very humble servant,

M. WASHINGTON

The generous sympathy expressed by the Senate and House of Representatives, together with the resolutions adopted by the citizens of Philadelphia and other places, have deeply affected my heart, and I feel myself bound by every tie of duty and gratitude to return my warmest acknowledgments for these distinguished honors rendered to the memory of the best and greatest man that ever lived. The extraordinary marks of respect shown on this melancholy occasion demonstrate the universal sense of his inestimable services, and will serve to console his surviving friends amid their irreparable loss. I am sensible that words are inadequate to express my feelings on this trying occasion, yet I cannot refrain from expressing my heartfelt thanks for the kind and generous manner in which you have been pleased to participate in my sorrow. That the Father of Mercies may support and comfort you under this and every other affliction, and finally receive us all into His holy kingdom, is the sincere prayer of your affectionate and obedient servant,

ABIGAIL ADAMS.

The nation has lost its father, and I have lost a friend whose kindness and counsel were never withheld from me through all the vicissitudes of public life. The testimonies I have received from every corner of our country have deeply moved my heart, and I pray that the Almighty will enable the bereaved nation to bear this heavy affliction with that resignation which becomes a Christian people.

You, Sir, who shared with him the cares and labors of establishing this republic, will best understand the value of his services and the magnitude of the loss we all deplore. I remain, with sentiments of the highest respect and esteem, your affectionate sister and friend,

ABIGAIL ADAMS.

pair.human_continuation:
Taught by the great example which I have so long had before me never
to oppose my private wishes to the public will, I must consent to the
request made by Congress, which you have had the goodness to transmit
to me; and in doing this I need not, I can not, say what a sacrifice
of individual feeling I make to a sense of public duty.

With grateful acknowledgments and unfeigned thanks for the personal
respect and evidences of condolence expressed by Congress and yourself,
I remain, very respectfully, sir, your most obedient, humble servant,

MARTHA WASHINGTON.



UNITED STATES, _January 13, 1800_.

_Gentlemen of the Senate and Gentlemen of the House of Representatives_:

A report made to me on the 5th of this month by the Secretary of War
contains various matters in which the honor and safety of the nation are
deeply interested.
pair.prefix:
JOHN ADAMS.



MOUNT VERNON, _December 31, 1799_.

The PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES.

SIR: While I feel with keenest anguish the late dispensation of Divine
Providence, I can not be insensible to the mournful tributes of respect
and veneration which are paid to the memory of my dear deceased husband;
and as his best services and most anxious wishes were always devoted to
the welfare and happiness of his country, to know that they were truly
appreciated and gratefully remembered affords no inconsiderable
consolation.
